issues.text: Whether the Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944 and the Rules framed thereunder and the Criminal Procedure Code maintain a distinction between the power to make a search and the manner of making it, such that the search by the Deputy Superintendent of Central Excise to gather information for imposing excise duty (and not for investigation of an offence) requires following s. 103 CrPC (general mode) and not s. 165 CrPC (for police officer during investigation of offence)?

Assuming s. 165 CrPC applies to the search, whether it confers power/jurisdiction on a police officer (extended to excise officer) and whether recording of reasons is a jurisdictional requirement or merely procedural, such that an excise officer deriving power under r. 201 of the Central Excise Rules need only follow the procedural part of s. 165?

arguments.claim: The Central Excise and Salt Act, 1944, the Rules framed thereunder, and the CrPC maintain a distinction between the power to make a search and the manner of making it, correlating specified power with particular procedure; since the search was to gather information for imposing excise duty not for prosecuting (investigation of offence), s.103 CrPC (general searches) applies, not s.165 CrPC (police officer during investigation of offence)

Assuming s.165 CrPC applies, the section confers power/jurisdiction on police officer to search and prescribes procedure; recording reasons relates to jurisdiction, so excise officer (with power from r.201 Central Excise Rules) need only follow procedural part of s.165, not jurisdictional recording
